entries.englishSourceDescription: Sitting on the ground, use a high cable in a single grip, to do lat pulldowns with a focus on a long stretch in the lats.
evidence: English and other translations explicitly describe floor-seated single-grip high-cable lat pulldowns, not a conventional horizontal row.
Source image 577 was inspected: one arm reaches toward a high pulley in a lat-stretch position. Lower body is cropped, so the image alone does not verify the floor setup.
API lists Cable machine and Incline bench; current catalog retained only Incline bench. The textual exercise does not use a bench.

recommendation.name: Single-arm high-cable pulldown
recommendation.guideText: Sit on the floor at a high cable pulley and hold its single grip in one hand. Begin with the working arm reaching toward the pulley so the lat is stretched. Pull the grip downward by bending the elbow, then return with control to the stretched position. Repeat on the other side.
recommendation.guideAuthorship: Independently authored factual description based on current wger movement text and inspected source image; retain original catalog source attribution.

entries.currentName: One Arm Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
entries.englishSourceDescription:
Set the pulley at the bottom of the cable machine and grab onto it without using any attachments. Extend the cable directly overhead.

While keeping your back straight and upper arm stationary, lower the cable behind your head until you feel a good stretch in your triceps, and then extend it back upward until your elbow is locked out.
evidence: Current API equipment is Cable machine only. English title and description agree on a one-arm overhead low-pulley cable triceps extension.
No source images or videos; no new attachment or stance requirements are inferred.
entries.condition: Keep the existing one-arm, low-pulley, no-attachment guide; preserve UUID and metric.

entries.englishSourceDescription: Using a medicine ball as an overload will make the exercise heavier.
evidence: English text only states that a medicine ball adds overload. API Bodyweight equipment is inconsistent with the exercise title and overload description.
Spanish translation 2560 explicitly identifies a medicine-ball V-up: supine straight legs, ball in both hands overhead, simultaneous legs/torso lift toward a V, controlled return.
Source image 671 inspected and agrees with that V-up motion. API flags this source image is_ai_generated=true; the illustration is corroboration, not sole movement evidence.

recommendation.guideText: Lie on your back with your legs straight and hold a medicine ball in both hands above and behind your head. Lift your legs and upper body together, bringing the ball toward your feet to form a V. Lower your legs and torso with control and repeat.
